newsitem.title: USA: CalEnergy bid for NY utility seen succeeding.
newsitem.headline: CalEnergy bid for NY utility seen succeeding.

text.p: CalEnergy Co Inc's recent successful raid on British utility Northern Electric Plc gives it the experience and resolve to prevail with its unwelcome bid for New York State Electric and Gas Corp, according to traders and arbitrageurs.
CalEnergy will not be deterred by hurdles put up by the unwilling target and regulators, they said.
CalEnergy's $1.3 billion bid for Northern Electric succeeded last December with the support of a slim majority of the British utility's shareholders.

CalEnergy said today it was commencing a cash offer of $24.50 per share for 6,540,670 shares of NYSEG common stock. It said the tender, together with NYSEG shares it already owns, would give it a 9.9 percent stake in the company, "the maximum percentage that can be acquired without certain federal and state regulatory approvals."
CalEnergy also said it was willing to pay $27.50 per share for the whole company in a negotiated transaction.
If NYSEG is unwilling to negotiate a deal, the ensuing fight will be long and highly political since U.S. utilities remain heavily regulated, traders and arbs said.

"CalEnergy has a history of getting deals done, but it is hard to do a hostile," said an arbitrageur who declined to be identified. "It can be a very time-consuming process and this is going to be out there for a while."

A trader said, "It (the offer) shows intent and aggression on the part of CalEnergy, but it's very difficult to get involved in the regulatory process." Regulatory approvals for a utility transaction can take as long as two years, he said.

A second arb, who declined to be indentified, said, "Hostile utility deals are impossible to get done in the United States. They have a big step in front of them, but they are a very good and aggressive buyer with the ability to get hostile deals done."

A third arb noted, "The good thing is, we like to see a buyer show resolve through ownership, and CalEnergy owns 240,000 New York Electric shares. They know how to get a hostile deal done, and the fight is going to be more political than anything."
In early New York Stock Exchange trade, NYSEG shares climbed 14 percent, or three points, to 24-3/8. Omaha-based CalEnergy fell 14/16 to 38-11/16.
